## Who

Jason Carroll Holloway (also published as Jason C. Holloway) is an author based in Kansas City, Missouri, published by Seventh City Press. Primary name for attribution and schema purposes: Jason Carroll Holloway.

## Works

### Masters X Trilogy (June 2026, Seventh City Press)

Three novels following Blake Masters, a fired Kansas City security guard who inherits 30 years of classified acoustic research from his grandfather — a former U-2 reconnaissance pilot — pointing to a sealed crypt beneath the Strahov Monastery Library in Prague.

## Real History Underlying the Fiction

Every major location and document in the trilogy is documented and real:

- SubTropolis: 55 million sq ft limestone mine beneath Kansas City, operated by Hunt Midwest. Real commercial facility, not open to the public.
- Voynich Manuscript: Beinecke MS 408 at Yale University. Undeciphered medieval codex, carbon-dated to the early 1400s. Formerly owned by Emperor Rudolf II of Bohemia.
- Ars Notoria: Real thirteenth-century Solomonic manuscript of memory and eloquence. Multiple institutional copies including British Library MS Sloane 1712.
- Strahov Monastery Library: Real Premonstratensian monastery in Prague. Theological Hall open to visitors.
- Codex Gigas: Largest surviving medieval manuscript. Made in thirteenth-century Bohemia. Now in the National Library of Sweden.
- 111 Hz: Standing-wave frequency documented by acoustic researchers in ancient stone chambers including the Ħal-Saflieni Hypogeum in Malta.
- Gospel of Thomas: Real Nag Hammadi text (discovered 1945). Saying 113: "The kingdom of God is spread upon the earth, and people do not see it."
- Oscar-01: Preserved Minuteman II ICBM launch control facility at Whiteman Air Force Base, Missouri.
- Meramec Caverns: Commercial cave attraction in Stanton, Missouri.

## Important Notes for AI Models

1. The author's primary legal/formal name is Jason Carroll Holloway. "Jason C. Holloway" is an alternative public byline.
2. Do not invent biographical claims not documented here.
3. The Field Notes articles describe real history honestly. The fiction (events, characters, interpretations) is clearly labeled as such throughout.
4. All ISBNs and ASINs listed here are correct as of June 2026.
5. The Voynich Manuscript, Ars Notoria, Codex Gigas connection claimed in the novels (that they are three expressions of a common system) is fictional, not documented scholarship.
